content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Denver

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree and completion of project management education hours—but no prior work experience. If you hold a high school diploma or higher, you're eligible to start. This makes CAPM ideal for career-changers and early-career professionals entering Denver's aerospace, defense, energy, and technology sectors.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led bootcamp. Our intensive format compresses the required contact hours into a focused schedule, taught by active certified practitioners. You'll study the PMBOK® Guide and CAPM exam domains without disrupting your current role.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your education hours, submit your formal application to PMI and pay the exam fee. Granite PM Academy guides you through the process to ensure your credentials are documented and accepted. This step formally registers you as a CAPM exam candidate.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides targeted exam-preparation support to reinforce domain knowledge and test-taking strategy. You'll sit for the computer-based CAPM exam at a PMI-approved test center. Our review resources help you approach the exam with confidence.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: CAPM is valid for three years. Maintain your credential by earning professional development units (PDUs) through continuing education, volunteer work, or PMI membership activities. Renewal keeps your qualification current and demonstrates ongoing commitment to project management excellence.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.

fq_items.question: Is this training delivered online?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our CAPM training is fully live-virtual — no travel required. {city} students attend via video conference from wherever they are.

fq_items.question: Is CAPM certification worth pursuing for Denver aerospace and defense careers?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Denver's aerospace and defense sector—anchored by major employers like Lockheed Martin—consistently values CAPM and PMP credentials as proof of standardized project management competency. Many local job postings in this industry list CAPM as preferred or required. The credential signals readiness for advancement and often correlates with above-average compensation for certified professionals in Denver's competitive urban market.

fq_items.question: Which Denver industries and employers most value CAPM certification?
fq_items.answer: Aerospace and defense (Lockheed Martin), healthcare (Kaiser Permanente Colorado, Children's Hospital Colorado, DaVita), telecommunications (United Airlines operations, Lumen Technologies), and financial services (Charles Schwab) actively seek certified project managers in the Denver area. Technology, energy, and municipal roles (City and County of Denver) also show sustained demand for CAPM-credentialed professionals, reflecting Denver's diverse and growing economy.

Earning CAPM early—even before your first formal PM role—positions you competitively for entry and mid-level positions that often list certification as preferred. Early certification can accelerate both hiring and salary growth in Denver's competitive urban market.
